description: The new non-CUDA row can contend with the existing non-CUDA row for a release asset name. Unlike the CUDA wheel command, the non-CUDA command passes no Torch-specific build tag, and the upload step allows overwrite.
trigger: Dispatch with release='1' and a parseable package version, with both Ubuntu/Python 3.11 non-CUDA builds producing a wheel under the same filename.
expected_behavior: If the non-CUDA jobs publish separate outputs, those outputs should have distinct asset names; if they are duplicate builds of one package, only one job needs to publish it.
actual_behavior: Both jobs select ./dist/*.whl and target the same versioned release with overwrite enabled. The workflow supplies no per-Torch discriminator or single-publisher guard on this path. No collision is implied if neither job emits a wheel or publication is disabled.

verification.description: Compared both non-CUDA rows with the build and upload steps. A whole-parent search for matrix.torch found Torch-dependent naming only in the job display name and the CUDA build tag, not in the non-CUDA build or upload naming.
verification.limits: Conditional on the backend emitting same-named wheels. Neither wheel generation nor concurrent upload behavior was tested.

introductions.rationale: Adds a second non-CUDA row with the same Ubuntu runner and Python 3.11 version. The inherited build and release steps supply no Torch-specific wheel tag for either row.
